question: Which of the following vedas about the treatment of diseases?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atharva Veda**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Atharva Veda is one of the four ancient sacred texts of **Hinduism**, alongside the **Rigveda, Yajurveda, and Samaveda**. It is the fourth Veda in the traditional classification.
 
• The Atharva Veda includes hymns, spells, and incantations **related to daily life,** health, healing, and protection from evil forces.
 
• In addition to its practical applications, the Atharva Veda also touches on philosophical concepts, such as the nature of the soul, the afterlife, and cosmology, contributing to Hindu spiritual thought.
 
• Composed in **Vedic Sanskrit**, the Atharva Veda is believed to have been compiled between **1000 BCE and 800 BCE**. It is divided into **20 books** (Kāṇḍas), with over 700 hymns and verses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Rig Veda**

 
• The Rig Veda is the** oldest of the four Vedas**, composed around **1500–1200 BCE**, and is one of the foundational texts of Hinduism.
 
• It contains over **1,000 hymns (suktas) **divided into **10 books (mandalas)**, dedicated to various deities like **Agni, Indra, and Soma**.
 
• The hymns are primarily prayers and praises meant for recitation during rituals, focusing on the forces of nature, cosmic order, and divine powers.

**Yajur Veda**

 
• The Yajur Veda primarily serves as a guide for performing Vedic rituals and sacrifices, offering detailed instructions for priests on how to conduct ceremonies.
 
• It is divided into two main versions, the **Shukla (White) Yajur Veda** and the **Krishna (Black) Yajur Veda**, differing in the organization and commentary of the hymns and prose.
 
• The text emphasizes offerings made to deities, the sacred fire, and the correct recitation of mantras during sacrificial rituals like the **Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice) and Agnihotra.**

**Sama Veda**

 
• The Sama Veda is known as the "**Veda of melodies**," consisting primarily of hymns and chants meant to be sung during rituals, making it the foundation of **Indian classical music.**
 
• Most of the verses in the Sama Veda are taken from the Rig Veda, but they are set to music and rhythm to be used in specific sacrificial ceremonies.
 
• It provides the musical framework for chanting mantras during important Vedic sacrifices, especially the **Soma sacrifice**, which involved offering a sacred drink.
